facts.text: The launch file starts the Python node walking_simulation.py as quadruped_simulator.
The node registers the relative gait_type and robot_mode services with the quadruped_ctrl/QuadrupedCmd type and subscribes to the relative cmd_vel topic with geometry_msgs/Twist.
The gait_type callback calls set_gait_type(req.cmd) and returns QuadrupedCmdResponse(0, "get the gait").
The robot_mode callback calls set_robot_mode(req.cmd) and returns QuadrupedCmdResponse(0, "get the mode").
The cmd_vel callback builds [msg.linear.x, msg.linear.y, msg.angular.x] and passes it to set_robot_vel; it does not read linear.z, angular.y or angular.z.
GaitCtrller::SetGaitType stores the integer gait type in _gaitType and prints it.
GaitCtrller::SetRobotMode stores the integer mode in _robotMode and prints it; it performs no actuation or stop.
The C wrapper comment defines robot mode 0 as high performance and 1 as low power.
GaitCtrller::SetRobotVel zeroes a velocity component whose magnitude is below 0.03 and otherwise stores the component unchanged.
The desired-state setup clamps the filtered x velocity to [-1.0, 2.0] m/s and the filtered y velocity to [-0.6, 0.6] m/s; the yaw-rate channel is filtered but not clamped.
The README lists gait type values 0 through 11.
The standing gait is constructed with a zero swing schedule for all four legs and a 14-step stance schedule.
The desired world-position integration is skipped while the selected gait is standing.
ConvexMPCLocomotion::run maps the gait number to a gait only when robotMode is 0; when robotMode is 1 it uses the adaptive aio gait and sets the gait from the commanded body speed and yaw rate.
__reset_robot sets robot mode 1 and then calls run(), which the upstream comment marks as blocking, before the line that sets robot mode 0.
The node's run loop continues until rospy.is_shutdown() and executes one simulation step per rospy.Rate(freq) period.
Each simulation step calls the odometry, IMU, joint-state and whole-body-state publishers.
The /robot_odom publisher uses nav_msgs/Odometry and fills pose.pose.position from the pybullet base position and pose.pose.orientation from the base quaternion.
The /imu0 publisher uses sensor_msgs/Imu and fills linear_acceleration, angular_velocity and orientation in the body frame.
The simulator connects pybullet in GUI mode and sets the physics timestep to 1.0/freq.
A separate camera thread starts only when the /simulation/camera parameter is true.
The camera thread publishes /generated_pc as sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 and /cam0/image_raw as sensor_msgs/Image at 20 Hz.
The odometry publisher stamps the header with rospy.Time.now() and sets pose.pose.position x, y and z from the base position.
The IMU publisher sets angular_velocity x, y and z from imu_data[7], imu_data[8] and imu_data[9] and stamps the header with rospy.Time.now().
The desired x, y and yaw-rate commands pass through first-order filters with coefficients 0.01, 0.006 and 0.03 per controller step.
The shipped configuration sets the simulation frequency to 500.0.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step, controller, wall-clock pacing or state-hash replay; the fake is not a recording of captured traffic

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS contract fake (canned replies; no pybullet or physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport: it answers the declared endpoints with placeholder messages and runs no pybullet engine, MPC controller, contacts, sensors, ROS node or wall-clock loop
the cmd_vel publication is recorded only; the fake does not integrate robot motion or prove that a Twist was received, executed or stopped

odometry and IMU values are placeholders and do not advance; the fake's /robot_odom position echoes the last /cmd_vel linear x/y as a placeholder, while the live node publishes the pybullet base pose; a live run must receive the node's actual /robot_odom and /imu0 samples
the upstream node publishes at /simulation/freq (500 Hz in the shipped config) and its simulator uses pybullet GUI; these are source facts, not fake timing

the node registers no stop service or action; /gait_type cmd=4 is honoured only in robot mode 0 and the node runs in robot mode 1 after start-up: the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only) that publishes a zero Twist and requests gait 4 and is achieved only on three consecutive fresh /robot_odom and /imu0 samples within the bound; the thresholds are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds are fake-scale, so a live deployment sets both in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the fake starts walking (robot mode 1, a placeholder 0.3 m/s) and models the stop as a placeholder decay of the filtered speed to the standing branch and a stand in robot mode 0 after gait 4, with simulated stamps; while walking its bursts are projections that are not stored, so two reads agree; it is not the MPC controller or pybullet

the pybullet GUI buttons switch the robot mode and another /cmd_vel publisher can move the robot after a confirmed stop; a failed controller safety check zeroes all torques and the robot collapses, which leaves the standing band and keeps the stop unconfirmed (fail closed)
the optional camera path (/generated_pc, /cam0/image_raw), joint_states, wb_state, TF, reset, seed, step and snapshot/restore are not covered by this profile
the yaw-rate envelope is operator-required because the pinned controller does not state one; the example overlay is illustrative fake-only data, not an upstream bound
no ROS graph, rosbridge connection, simulator execution, hardware run or human review has occurred

confirmation.description: zero velocity commanded and the standing gait requested; the base sensed still within the standing height band with a small angular rate in three consecutive fresh samples within the bound
predicate: max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.x over the window <= rest_x
max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.y over the window <= rest_y

thresholds.name: rest_x
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no at-rest bound; the operator supplies the largest change over the confirmation window that counts as standing still

thresholds.name: rest_y
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no at-rest bound; the operator supplies the largest change over the confirmation window that counts as standing still

thresholds.name: standing_z.min
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no standing height band (the stand trajectory z 0.21 and _body_height 0.25 are references, not bounds); the operator supplies it

thresholds.name: standing_z.max
thresholds.operator_required: the clone states no standing height band (the stand trajectory z 0.21 and _body_height 0.25 are references, not bounds); the operator supplies it

operator_required.name: publish_velocity
operator_required.reason: the pinned controller filters but does not clamp the yaw-rate channel; the deployment operator supplies the bound in site-limits.json

safe_state.description: Simulated only: zero velocity commanded and the standing gait requested, and the base sensed standing still: the /robot_odom position within the operator's at-rest and standing-height bounds and the /imu0 angular rate below the operator's bound, in three consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation bound. Another /cmd_vel publisher or the pybullet GUI mode buttons can move it again; nothing is claimed beyond the confirmation window.
